archetypes.name: verbatim-extract
archetypes.rationale: Validates that the plan's byte-identical move claim is fully specified and testable — subtle heredoc-vs-file differences (shebang, docstring, PEP 585 annotations) could silently break the invariant.
archetypes.prompt_body: Inspect the plan's specification that dedup-plan-lines.py is a 'verbatim move' from the plan-review-loop.sh heredoc (lines 501-580). Verify the plan correctly accounts for every Python construct it names (heading_re, fence_re, norm_key, update_heading_state, two-pass in_fence_lines, Constraints protection) and that adding a shebang and module docstring cannot alter runtime behavior. Check whether the plan's testing strategy — existing dedup assertions plus a manual spot-check — is actually sufficient to detect any inadvertent semantic drift, or whether an automated diff-based check is missing. Assess whether the PEP 585 annotation edge case (set[int], list[tuple[int,int]] requiring Python 3.9+) is present in the actual heredoc or merely inferred, and whether the plan specifies how to surface a version-mismatch failure. Cite specific file paths and line ranges for any issues found, and follow the output-format rules from your outer wrapper exactly.

archetypes.name: eval-isolation-completeness
archetypes.rationale: The plan requires coordinated export-list additions across 4 test locations plus their inner bash -c lists; a single omission silently fails under set -u, and the non-numeric stub shape change adds another failure path.
archetypes.prompt_body: Verify that the plan explicitly covers every one of the four awk-extraction test sites (near lines 1746, 1797, 1836, 1878 of test-plan-review-loop.sh) for both the outer export and the inner bash -c export list — a missed export in any of the eight spots causes a set -u abort that the plan's testing strategy may not clearly surface. Check the plan's description of changing the non-numeric python3 stub from a heredoc-era stdin-reading shape to a deterministic bogus-output stub: does it name the exact file and block that needs changing, or leave the target ambiguous? Assess whether the REAL_PYTHON capture-before-PATH-mutation requirement is specified precisely enough to prevent wrapper recursion under all PYWRAP invocation shapes the integration test will exercise. Cite specific file paths and line ranges for any issues found, and follow the output-format rules from your outer wrapper exactly.

archetypes.name: lint-graph-coverage
archetypes.rationale: The plan relies on agent-lint.toml exclusions to prevent dead-script failures, but if the exclusion syntax or comment convention does not match the existing lint graph, relevant-checks.sh will reject the new helper as unreferenced.
archetypes.prompt_body: Examine the plan's agent-lint.toml change specification: does it identify the exact exclusion block the new helper and sibling .md should join, and does the proposed comment form (naming plan-review-loop.sh as the runtime caller) match the style of existing entries in that block? Verify the plan does not conflate the script-md-siblings sibling-existence rule with the dead-script exclusion — if they are enforced by different mechanisms, both must be addressed. Check whether the variableized caller path form ($DEDUP_PLAN_LINES_PY in plan-review-loop.sh) is one the lint graph can statically trace, or whether an exclusion is definitely required rather than conditionally required. Assess whether the plan's parse-plan-commands.md cross-reference addition is precise enough that markdownlint and the sibling-doc rule will both pass without additional config. Cite specific file paths and line ranges for any issues found, and follow the output-format rules from your outer wrapper exactly.
